title: Converse to Theorem 1.1 (3-Coloring dichotomy for $H$-free graphs)
statement_text: If every component of $H$ is a path, then the $3$-Coloring Problem restricted to $H$-free graphs can be solved in polynomial time.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple. A graph $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. The $k$-Coloring Problem asks whether an input graph has a proper colouring with $k$ colours; the List-$k$-Coloring Problem asks, given $G$ and lists $L(v)\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}$, whether $G$ has a proper colouring with each $v$ coloured from $L(v)$. $rP_s$ denotes the disjoint union of $r$ paths on $s$ vertices and $H_1+H_2$ the disjoint union. Holyer, and Kamiński and Lozin, proved that if $H$ has a component which is not a path, then 3-Coloring is NP-hard on $H$-free graphs (via claws, i.e. line graphs, and via graphs of large girth). The statement is the converse, which the paper describes as wide open rather than conjecturing it; it asks whether 3-Coloring is polynomial-time solvable on $H$-free graphs whenever $H$ is a linear forest (disjoint union of paths), so that the 'easy' and 'hard' cases of $H$ would be completely distinguished for $k=3$. The paper itself settles the analogous dichotomy for List-$k$-Coloring for every $k>4$: it is polynomial on $H$-free graphs if $H$ is an induced subgraph of $rP_3$ or of $P_5+rP_1$ for some $r$, and NP-hard otherwise (assuming P $\ne$ NP); in particular List-$k$-Coloring is polynomial on $rP_3$-free graphs for all fixed $k,r$.
notes: Not a labelled environment; the open problem is identified by the remark 'The converse to Theorem 1.1 is wide open.' The statement of the converse is implicit and reconstructed from Theorem 1.1.

title: Full dichotomy for $k$-Coloring on $H$-free graphs ($k\geq 3$)
statement_text: For every integer $k \geq 3$, characterise the graphs $H$ for which the $k$-Coloring Problem restricted to $H$-free graphs is polynomial-time solvable versus NP-hard.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple. A graph $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. The $k$-Coloring Problem asks whether an input graph has a proper colouring with $k$ colours; the List-$k$-Coloring Problem asks, given $G$ and lists $L(v)\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}$, whether $G$ has a proper colouring with each $v$ coloured from $L(v)$. $rP_s$ denotes the disjoint union of $r$ paths on $s$ vertices and $H_1+H_2$ the disjoint union. For 3-Coloring, Holyer and Kamiński–Lozin showed NP-hardness on $H$-free graphs whenever some component of $H$ is not a path, and the converse is wide open; in general, for the $k$-Coloring Problem no value $k\ge3$ is known for which the polynomial cases of $H$ are completely separated from the NP-hard ones. For List-$k$-Coloring this was also the case until Hajebi, Li and Spirkl settled $k=5$, and the present paper settles all $k>4$: assuming P $\ne$ NP, List-$k$-Coloring on $H$-free graphs is polynomial if and only if $H$ is an induced subgraph of $rP_3$ or of $P_5+rP_1$ for some $r\ge1$ (NP-hardness coming from $P_6$ for $k>3$ and $P_4+P_2$ for $k>4$).
